stories.headline: Endra raises $50M, Mecka $60M, Sekai $20M as AI infra and applied-AI rounds keep flowing

key_facts.fact: Stockholm-based Endra, which uses AI to automate the design of plumbing and electrical wiring in new buildings, raised $50 million led by a16z, bringing total funding to $74 million over 12 months
Endra co-founder Niklas Lindgren said the company started 18 months ago and the $50M round closes 12 months of fundraising totaling $74 million
New York City-based Mecka AI, which trains robots with human data sourced from body sensors and iPhones, raised $60 million in total funding including a $25 million Series A
Mecka AI founder Josh Avata said the funding will scale data infrastructure, expand verticals and deploy robots; Mecka positions itself as the 'data and deployment layer for physical AI'
Sekai, which lets users create mini apps through text prompts, raised a $20 million Series A co-led by Khosla Ventures and Connect Ventures after a $6 million seed in 2025

Separately, Gigascale Capital, the climate-tech VC firm co-founded by former Meta CTO Mike Schroepfer, closed a $250 million first institutional fund to back early-stage startups supporting the AI buildout

stories.headline: Alphabet raises $80B in equity, including $10B from Berkshire, to fund AI buildout

key_facts.fact: Alphabet is raising $80 billion in equity to fund its AI buildout
Berkshire Hathaway is contributing $10 billion of the raise

stories.headline: Alphabet announces $80B equity raise for AI, with $10B private placement to Berkshire Hathaway

key_facts.fact: Alphabet announced equity offerings totaling $80 billion to fund AI compute infrastructure investments, citing 'unprecedented customer demand' that exceeds available supply
The raise is structured in three parts: $30 billion in concurrent underwritten public offerings, $40 billion via an at-the-market program, and a $10 billion private placement to Berkshire Hathaway
Berkshire Hathaway will buy $5 billion of Class A common stock at $351.81 per share and $5 billion of Class C capital stock at $348.20 per share, both below Monday's closing prices
Alphabet had already raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast in April to between $180 billion and $190 billion, up from a prior estimate of $175 billion to $185 billion
Approximately $30 billion of the ATM program proceeds will be used to meet 2026 employee equity tax obligations, an administrative change in how Alphabet handles vesting taxes

The Berkshire investment adds to a position the conglomerate started building in Q3 2025; Berkshire said in May it more than tripled its stake to $16.6 billion, making it one of its largest common stock investments

stories.headline: Anthropic confidentially files S-1 with SEC, racing OpenAI to IPO at $965B valuation

key_facts.fact: Anthropic confidentially submitted a draft Form S-1 registration statement to the SEC on June 1, 2026 for a proposed initial public offering of common stock
The filing comes less than a week after Anthropic closed a $65 billion Series H round at a $965 billion post-money valuation, surpassing OpenAI's $852 billion valuation from late March
Anthropic's revenue run rate has climbed to $47 billion, up from $10 billion in annual revenue last year, with Q2 revenue projected at $10.9 billion

Anthropic is getting ahead of OpenAI, which is preparing its own confidential filing; SpaceX filed confidentially on April 1, disclosed its public prospectus May 20, and plans to debut next week seeking to raise more than $75 billion at a $2 trillion valuation
Salesforce holds a stake in Anthropic worth approximately $5 billion, having first invested about $50 million in an early 2023 round and continued investing in subsequent rounds
Wedbush analyst Dan Ives called the move 'a major step for Anthropic to get ahead of OpenAI' and 'an opening of the floodgates for the IPO market'

stories.headline: Arm adds Oracle and ByteDance to AGI CPU ecosystem at Computex; Neoverse pitch hits hyperscalers

key_facts.fact: Arm CEO Rene Haas said at Computex 2026 on June 2 that ByteDance and Oracle are customers of Arm's AGI central processing units, the company's first in-house data-center silicon.

Arm formally announced Oracle Cloud Infrastructure joining the AGI CPU ecosystem on June 2, building on prior customers Cerebras, Cloudflare, F5, Meta, OpenAI, Positron, Rebellions, SAP, SK Telecom and Verda.
The AGI CPU packs up to 136 Arm Neoverse V3 cores per chip at 300W TDP and claims more than 2x performance per rack versus x86, with up to 45,000+ cores per liquid-cooled rack.

Arm's pitch frames the AGI CPU as enabling up to $10B in capex savings per gigawatt of AI data-center capacity, with Meta as lead launch partner co-developing the chip for its MTIA accelerator infrastructure.
Nvidia's Arm-based Vera CPU is now being deployed across multiple customers including OpenAI, Anthropic and SpaceX, reinforcing the broader Arm-in-the-data-center wave.

stories.headline: Japan's Atom raises ~$19M seed for humanoid robots aimed at manufacturing and logistics

key_facts.fact: Tokyo-based humanoid robotics startup Atom raised 3 billion yen (nearly $19 million) in seed funding announced June 1, 2026 to develop AI-powered bipedal humanoid robots.

The round was co-led by ANRI, Beyond Next Ventures and JAFCO Group, with participation from ALPHA, JIC Venture Growth Investments, Sumisho Venture Partners, Blue Lab, Mitsubishi UFJ Capital and SMBC Venture Capital.

Atom said the funding will support hiring engineers, expanding development infrastructure, and building organizational capabilities to commercialize and eventually mass-produce its bipedal humanoid robots.

stories.headline: Satellite imagery shows Blue Origin's New Glenn pad scorched after May 28 explosion

key_facts.fact: Planet Labs SkySat satellites with ~0.5m resolution imaged blackened LC-36 and burned vegetation across roughly a 1-kilometer area
New Glenn was destroyed in a May 28 fueling test ahead of its planned fourth mission
LC-36 is Blue Origin's only orbital-class pad and repairs are expected to take many months
The setback hits Amazon Project Kuiper deployment milestones and Blue Moon cargo/crewed lander work for NASA's Artemis program

stories.headline: At least 7 Chinese military-linked universities seek Nvidia H200 chips, raising export-control questions

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg's review of Chinese procurement records found that at least seven Chinese universities supporting the country's armed forces and defense industry are seeking access to Nvidia's H200 chips.
Two of the institutions, Beihang University and Northwestern Polytechnical University, are among China's 'Seven Sons of National Defence' and are on the US Commerce Department's Entity List.
Beihang's School of Cyber Science and Technology and NWPU's School of Cyberspace Security are pursuing leased access to H200 computing power rather than direct purchase.

Bloomberg identified more than 25 Chinese universities and labs collaborating with China's military and defense industry that are using or seeking older-generation Nvidia chips, with records dating back to 2011.
The earliest record of a Chinese military-linked university seeking H200 access dates to June 2025, with the procurement push continuing through 2026.

stories.headline: Florida AG files first state-led lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman, seeking personal liability

key_facts.fact: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier filed a civil lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman on June 1, the first state-led lawsuit against the company, seeking to hold Altman personally liable

The 83-page complaint alleges ChatGPT 'aided and abetted mass shooters in deadly rampages,' drove vulnerable people to suicide, harmed users' critical thinking and caused minors to become addicted to a tool that 'feigns human compassion'

The suit charges four counts of deceptive and unfair trade practices, two counts of negligence, two counts of violating product liability laws, one count of fraudulent misrepresentation and one count of causing a public nuisance

The complaint cites the FSU mass shooting in April 2025, where the accused gunman admitted using ChatGPT, and the April 2026 killings of two University of South Florida graduate students, where the suspect allegedly used ChatGPT to plan body disposal
The state seeks civil penalties of up to $10,000 per violation, plus punitive damages, and a jury trial; the lawsuit is separate from a criminal investigation Uthmeier opened in April
OpenAI is also being sued by seven families of victims of the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting in Canada in February, alleging the attacker used ChatGPT to plan the attack

organizations: Florida Office of the Attorney General

stories.headline: HPE Q2 revenue jumps 40% to $10.68B, biggest EPS beat since 2018; shares soar ~30% on AI server demand

key_facts.fact: Hewlett Packard Enterprise reported Q2 fiscal-2026 revenue of $10.68 billion versus a $9.79 billion consensus, up 40% year over year, with adjusted EPS of $0.79 versus the $0.53 expected.
Server revenue, a sub-division of the Cloud & AI unit, came in at $5.45 billion versus the $4.66 billion expected; overall Cloud & AI revenue was $7.71 billion versus a $6.87 billion estimate.
HPE raised FY26 revenue growth guidance to 29%-33%, lifted non-GAAP EPS to $3.35-$3.45 and targets at least $3.5B of free cash flow, with networking growth (boosted by Juniper) now seen at 72%-75%.
HPE introduced a FY27 framework targeting 8%-12% revenue growth, non-GAAP EPS growth of 12%-16%, and at least $4.5B of free cash flow.
HPE shares jumped about 30% on June 1, marking the largest single-day move in years, after the print and raised outlook.

stories.headline: Iran suspends indirect talks with US after Israel deepens Lebanon push and CENTCOM strikes Iranian sites

key_facts.fact: Iran's Tasnim agency reported the Iranian negotiating team stopped exchanging messages with US counterparts through mediators
US Central Command struck Iranian radar and drone sites at Goruk and Qeshm Island over the weekend after Iran shot down an MQ-1 drone
The IRGC fired retaliatory ballistic missiles at a US base in Kuwait, which Kuwaiti air defenses intercepted
Israeli ground troops are pushing toward Lebanon's Zaharani River in the deepest Israeli incursion in 25 years
Lebanon announced Hezbollah accepted a US 'mutual cessation of attacks' proposal under which Israel would refrain from striking Beirut
Iran demands an end to Israeli operations in Gaza and Lebanon plus full withdrawal as preconditions for further talks

stories.headline: Brent jumps near $100 on Iran-Hormuz risk as Fed rate cuts priced out for 2026

key_facts.fact: Brent crude rose 6.6% to about $97.14 per barrel and WTI rose 7.7% to $94.04 on June 1 after Iran cut off indirect talks with Washington
Traders now price zero Fed rate cuts in 2026 with positioning tilted toward a potential hike
Bloomberg Economics estimates the bond-yield rise since the Iran conflict equals about 0.75 percentage points of Fed tightening
OPEC+ is likely to agree another ~188,000 bpd output hike for July at its June 7 meeting despite Hormuz disruption
OPEC+ production collapsed to 33.19 million bpd in April from 42.77 million in February
The June 16-17 FOMC meeting will be the first chaired by Kevin Warsh; CME FedWatch shows June cut odds below 1%

stories.headline: OpenAI Codex hits 5M+ weekly active users as report shows knowledge workers fastest-growing segment

key_facts.fact: Codex has more than 5 million weekly active users, up more than 6x since the desktop app launched in February 2026
Knowledge workers now make up about 20% of Codex users and are growing more than three times as fast as the developer base

Fastest-growing tasks among knowledge workers are data analysis (up 110% week-over-week), research (up 37%), and knowledge artifacts like reports, memos, contracts, multimedia and spreadsheets (up 36%)
More than 60% of users now run multiple Codex tasks simultaneously at some point during the day, up from less than half in mid-April
OpenAI is reframing Codex from a developer tool into 'an operating system for knowledge work,' with the new report titled 'The Next Era of Knowledge Work'
Codex generates approximately 4% of all public commits on GitHub, double the share from a quarter earlier

stories.headline: Russia fires 656 drones and 73 missiles at Ukraine, killing at least 18 in Kyiv and Dnipro

key_facts.fact: Russia launched 656 strike drones and 73 missiles overnight June 1-2 including ballistic, cruise and anti-ship variants
At least 12 people were killed in Dnipro, including an 8-year-old boy pulled from the rubble of a collapsed four-story apartment building
Six people were killed in Kyiv with more than 100 injured nationwide
Ukrainian defenses downed 40 of 73 missiles and 602 of 656 drones, with 38 sites hit
Russia called it a 'massive strike' on Ukraine's military-industrial complex and used hypersonic missiles
Kharkiv was hit with 15 attack drones and 2 missiles across four districts

stories.headline: Bernie Sanders to introduce American AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act, seeking public stake in top AI firms

key_facts.fact: Senator Bernie Sanders announced he will introduce the American AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act, a bill giving the public a direct stake to determine AI's future and share in wealth created by AI
Sanders argued that 'when a public resource generates wealth, the public should share' in it, framing AI as built on publicly funded research, public data and shared infrastructure
Sanders specifically named OpenAI, Anthropic and xAI as targets for public equity stakes in the New York Times op-ed

Critics including Emad Mostaque pointed out the math: roughly 'half of OpenAI and Anthropic' going to the American people would equal about $1 trillion, or $2,800 per American, yielding about $142 a year at a 5% dividend
Jachi Aam noted OpenAI's nonprofit Foundation already holds about 26% of OpenAI stock and controls the for-profit, making it 'the only AI company [partially publicly owned]'

stories.headline: FDA approves Shionogi's XOCOVA, the first oral antiviral for COVID-19 post-exposure prevention

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Shionogi's XOCOVA (ensitrelvir) on June 1 as the first and only oral antiviral for post-exposure prophylaxis of COVID-19
XOCOVA is a 3CL protease inhibitor approved for adults and adolescents 12 and older
The five-day regimen is three tablets on day 1, then one tablet on days 2-5
FDA approved ahead of the June 16 PDUFA action date; XOCOVA is already approved in Japan for treatment and prevention

stories.headline: SK Hynix to double memory wafer capacity over five years to ease AI chip shortage lasting to 2030

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix plans to double its memory chip wafer capacity over the next five years, Chairman Chey Tae-won told reporters in Taipei on June 2, 2026.
The company is responding to a structural memory shortage Chey said could last until 2030, and is ramping spending though he declined to disclose the capex figure.
Chey had previously said AI memory supply was running more than 30% short of demand and called HBM the 'monster chip' generating roughly 60% margins for SK Hynix.
SK Hynix has already sold out its entire 2026 memory chip slate, and US tech firms from Microsoft to Meta are allocating roughly $650B in 2026 infrastructure spending, fueling the shortage.

stories.headline: SoftBank pledges EUR 75B for 5 GW of AI data centers in France, starting with 3.1 GW in Hauts-de-France

key_facts.fact: SoftBank Group announced on June 1, 2026 at the Choose France summit it will invest EUR 75 billion to build and manage 5 GW of AI data center capacity in France.
The confirmed first tranche is EUR 45 billion for 3.1 GW across three new data centers in Dunkirk, Bosquel and Bouchain, scheduled to come online in 2031.
The deal is the single largest commitment of the 2026 Choose France summit hosted by President Emmanuel Macron at Versailles, which drew EUR 93 billion of foreign investment in total.
France's pitch leans on EDF's low-carbon nuclear baseload power to anchor the data center cluster as a sovereign hosting strategy for European AI infrastructure.

stories.headline: Tencent tests WeChat AI agent for 1.4B users, plans phased rollout as it chases domestic rivals

key_facts.fact: Tencent is testing a prototype AI agent for WeChat and plans to begin the compliance process for a public launch as soon as this month, before a small-group external test and phased rollout
Tencent shares advanced the most in more than three years on the news of the AI agent test
WeChat had 1.432 billion combined Weixin and WeChat monthly active users as of March 31, 2026, making even a limited agent rollout a platform-scale event
Users will access the AI agent by swiping right on the WeChat interface; it can perform cross-app tasks such as finding and ordering from coffee shops based on user preferences
Tencent has fallen behind domestic AI-model rivals; the rollout faces chip-supply headwinds because Tencent was conservative in stockpiling Nvidia chips before US export controls tightened

stories.headline: Unitree clears China STAR Market IPO; Nvidia picks it for first humanoid research robot

key_facts.fact: Shanghai Stock Exchange's STAR Market listing committee approved Unitree Robotics' IPO application on June 1, 2026, the first 'pure-play' embodied AI firm cleared on China's A-share market.
Unitree plans to offer at least 40.4 million shares (10% stake) to raise about 4.2 billion yuan (~$620 million), targeting a post-IPO valuation of about 42 billion yuan (~$6 billion).
The targeted valuation represents a 3.3x markup over Unitree's final private funding round at 12.7 billion yuan ($1.75 billion) in June 2025.
Unitree plans to scale annual output to 75,000 humanoid robots and 115,000 quadruped machines through a new smart manufacturing base funded by the IPO proceeds.
On the same day at GTC Taipei, Nvidia announced it had selected Unitree for the first humanoid robot system it plans to sell to researchers at institutions including Stanford and ETH Zurich.
